defects: Does not reference `totalVariation` or the Hahn–Jordan decomposition at all — the entire point of the informal statement (that two independently-defined notions of total variation coincide) is lost; the produced statement only presents the partition-supremum side.

Changes the statement's shape from a single global equality of measures `μ.totalVariation = μ.variation` to a pointwise claim universally quantified over every measurable set A with an added `MeasurableSet A` hypothesis not present in the gold.

If `SignedMeasure.variation` is already defined (as in Mathlib) via this supremum formula, the produced theorem is a trivial/definitional restatement rather than the substantive equivalence with the Hahn-Jordan-based `totalVariation` that the gold asserts.

Uses `Finpartition A` and `∑ B in p.parts, |s B|` as an ad hoc reformulation instead of the actual Mathlib `variation`/`totalVariation` definitions, so it is unclear this matches the real definitions/signatures used by Mathlib, risking a mismatched or non-existent formalization of the partition-supremum notion.

Theorem name and signature bear no resemblance to the gold `totalVariation_eq_variation`, and introduce a differently-typed conclusion (an equation about applying variation to a set with `|s B|` sums) rather than an equation of two `Measure X` objects.
